correctness.summary: Cycle-block distances are ambient-distance preserving, so every cycle block of length at least six contributes an explicit induced hole to the square. Conversely, when all non-complete cycle blocks are C4 or C5, leaf-block peeling gives explicit simplicial orders for clique, C4, and C5 blocks and hence a perfect-elimination ordering of the whole square.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Exact and synonymous searches, the accessible full text of the recent cactus-square coloring paper, the open cactus-root paper, and the block-graph-square endpoint found no five-cycle chordality threshold. Ducoffe 2019 is the principal residual risk because only its abstract and accessible summaries, not the full journal theorem text, were inspected.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact sharp structural boundary for chordality of squares on the standard cactus-block class, extends the classical tree/block-graph endpoint, and supplies a constructive perfect-elimination ordering with C6 as the first obstruction.

limitations: The cactus-block root is assumed given; this is not a new square-root recognition algorithm.
Strong chordality is not characterized and can fail even when all cycle blocks have length at most five.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the uninspected full Ducoffe 2019 theorem text and older terminology remain residual coverage risks.
Independent audit has not been performed.
